chunks: "I think of it as a chain. First, dissipate less: if an LDO is burning 0. 85 watts dropping 5 volts to 3. 3 volts at half an amp, a buck converter at 90% efficiency burns about 0.
18 watts, so the best thermal fix is sometimes a different part. Then I give the heat a good way out.

For a package with an exposed pad, I solder the pad to a copper area on the top layer with a solid connection, not a thermal relief, and add an array of thermal vias, say 9 to 12 small ones, to inner planes and the bottom layer.
I use as much copper area as I can, on both sides, and heavier copper if needed, because copper spreads heat about a thousand times better than FR-4.
It all ends up in the air, so board area and airflow set the final temperature: roughly 20 K/W for a 50 by 50 mm board in still air.

Also placement: spread the hot parts apart, put them near the board edge or in the airflow, keep them away from temperature-sensitive parts like references, crystals, electrolytic capacitors and sensors, and don't stack them.
And if the board alone isn't enough, I'll add a heat sink or spread into the enclosure. Then I check with a thermal camera."
